cards.d: If someone acts accordingly, they act in a way that is suitable.
cards.e: He feels like he did a good job, and his boss should pay him accordingly.

cards.d: An anchor is a heavy object dropped from a boat to make it stay in one place.
cards.e: When the ship reached its destination, the crew dropped the anchor.

cards.d: A buoy is a floating sign that warns boats of dangerous areas.
cards.e: Don’t steer the boat near those buoys. There are rocks underneath the water.

cards.d: A catastrophe is an unexpected event that causes great suffering or damage.
cards.e: It was a catastrophe for my family when my dad lost his job.

cards.d: Context is the situations that form the background of an event.
cards.e: They studied the context of the battle before giving their presentation.

cards.d: To designate someone or something means to give them a particular description.
cards.e: The famous lighthouse was designated a historical monument.

cards.d: To distort something means to lie about it.
cards.e: His lawyer distorted the facts so that he would be set free.

cards.d: A dock is an enclosed area where ships go to be loaded, unloaded, and repaired.
cards.e: The huge ship pulled into the dock, and the crew unloaded the cargo.

cards.d: The fore of something is the front part of it.
cards.e: The teacher’s desk is at the fore of the classroom.

cards.d: If something is frequent, then it happens or is done often.
cards.e: While Dad was sick, the doctor made frequent visits to his house.

cards.d: When something is genuine, it is true or real.
cards.e: After the painting was determined to be genuine, it sold for a million dollars.

cards.d: Grease is an oily substance put on moving parts, so they work smoothly.
cards.e: When I was done working on the car, I had grease all over my hands.

cards.d: When something is intricate, it has many small parts or details.
cards.e: The intricate painting on the quilt was very lovely.

cards.d: To offset means to use one thing to cancel out the effect of another thing.
cards.e: Increased wages are offset by higher prices for goods.

cards.d: To overlap something means to cover a piece of it.
cards.e: The gift on top overlaps the other gift on the bottom.

cards.d: To precipitate an event means to cause it to happen sooner than normal.
cards.e: The violent attack precipitated an all-out war.

cards.d: When something is secondhand, it has been owned by someone else.
cards.e: Her secondhand jeans were a bit faded in the front.

cards.d: A slot is a narrow opening in a machine or container.
cards.e: To operate the machine, put your coins into the slot.

cards.d: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid.
cards.e: The whale submerged its huge body into the ocean.

cards.d: A tactic is a careful plan to achieve something.
cards.e: Sam thought of a good tactic in order to attract more business.
